title: Why granite has big crystals and basalt small ones
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does granite have big crystals?
What is the difference between granite and basalt?

explain.say: Granite and basalt are both igneous rocks, made when melted rock cools and hardens. Yet granite is speckled with big crystals, and basalt looks smooth and dark.

draw.text: Why granite has big crystals and basalt small ones

explain.say: Granite forms from magma trapped deep underground, wrapped in warm rock like a blanket. It cools over thousands of years, giving crystals plenty of time to grow big.

Basalt forms from lava that erupts onto the surface and cools in days or weeks. The crystals have no time to grow, so they stay tiny. Lava cooled instantly can even become glass with no crystals at all.
So you can read a rock's past from its crystals: big crystals mean slow cooling underground, tiny crystals mean fast cooling at the surface.

faq.q: Why does granite have big crystals?
faq.a: Granite cooled slowly from magma deep underground, over thousands of years. Slow cooling gave the atoms time to gather into large crystals you can see.
Basalt forms when runny lava erupts and cools quickly at the surface, often from volcanoes on ocean floors or in places like Hawaii and Iceland. Most of the ocean floor is basalt.

faq.q: What is the difference between intrusive and extrusive rock?
faq.a: Intrusive igneous rock, like granite, cooled inside the Earth. Extrusive igneous rock, like basalt, cooled on the surface from lava.
Obsidian is volcanic glass. It forms when lava cools so fast that no crystals grow at all, leaving a shiny black glass with very sharp edges.

faq.q: Why is basalt darker than granite?
faq.a: Basalt is rich in iron and magnesium minerals, which are dark. Granite has lots of quartz and feldspar, which are light-coloured.

facts: Most of the ocean floor is made of basalt.
The Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland is made of basalt columns formed as lava cooled and cracked.

quiz.say: A rock has crystals too small to see. How did it most likely cool?
quiz.why: Fast cooling, as with lava at the surface, gives crystals no time to grow.

wrong.1: Slow cooling underground makes big crystals, as in granite.
wrong.2: Igneous rocks form from melted rock, so it did melt.
